product: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 Portable Power Station (2,073.6 Wh LiFePO4, 2,600 W)

price_today.value: $899.00 (compare-at $899.00, in stock); $854.05 with code DEALECTRIC (5%). Kits on the same store: + 200 W panel $1,199.00, + 2 × 200 W panels $1,499.00, both available

wins.need: Leaving the AC outlets on all day or overnight (fridge, CPAP, router, a reptile heater)
wins.claim: The Solar Lab ran the same test on all four units. The Elite 200 V2 had the lowest idle draw with the inverter on: 9.5 W, against 17 W for the Jackery Explorer 2000 v2, about 18 W for the Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 (AC outlets on standby) and about 27 W for the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max. Arithmetic over 24 h: 228 Wh (Elite), 408 Wh (Jackery), 432 Wh (Anker), 648 Wh (EcoFlow). That is about 11% of the Elite's rated capacity against about 32% of the DELTA 3 Max's. CleanTechnica found a similar figure: 40% to 34% in 12 h with nothing plugged in, about 10.4 W (arithmetic).
wins.who: The Solar Lab (measured, no author or date on the pages); CleanTechnica (Z. S., 2025-07-07); arithmetic by Dealectric

wins.need: Getting the most usable energy out of the battery
wins.claim: The Solar Lab measured these efficiencies: Elite 200 V2 94%, Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 90%, Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 about 89%, EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max 79%. In APH Networks' drain test with a steady 987 W heater, the Elite delivered 2,028 Wh, 97.8% of its rating.
wins.who: The Solar Lab; APH Networks (Jonathan Kwan, 2025-02-21)

wins.claim: The Elite 200 V2 takes up to 1,000 W of solar input (12–60 V, 20 A). The Solar Lab gives the rivals' limits as 500 W (DELTA 3 Max), 400 W (Jackery Explorer 2000 v2) and 800 W (Anker C2000 Gen 2). Arithmetic for the fastest possible solar refill of rated capacity at each limit: about 2.1 h (Elite), 2.6 h (Anker), 4.1 h (EcoFlow), 5.1 h (Jackery). In real use, CleanTechnica measured 520–600 W in sun and 25% to 100% from 12:00 to 3:39 pm. The Solar Lab saw up to 800 W.
wins.who: BLUETTI (spec); The Solar Lab (rival specs, measured peak); CleanTechnica (measured); arithmetic

wins.need: Running large appliances at the same time
wins.claim: The Elite is rated for 2,600 W continuous. The rivals' makers rate theirs lower: DELTA 3 Max 2,400 W, Anker C2000 Gen 2 2,400 W, Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 2,200 W. The Solar Lab ran the Elite at 3,000 W for more than 2 minutes. CleanTechnica ran a 953 W portable AC, a 1,345 W Keurig and a 1,482 W air fryer on it without trouble.
wins.who: Maker specs; The Solar Lab and CleanTechnica (measured loads)

wins.claim: At list price the Elite costs $0.43 per rated Wh, effectively tied with the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max ($879 / 2,048 Wh = $0.43). It is cheaper than the Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 ($999 / 2,042 Wh = $0.49) and the Anker C2000 Gen 2 at anker.com's $1,499 ($0.73). With code DEALECTRIC it is $854.05, or $0.41 per rated Wh. Against APH's measured 2,028 Wh, the list price works out to $0.44 per usable Wh.
wins.who: Arithmetic on maker store prices read today

wins.need: A battery that lasts many years
wins.claim: BLUETTI rates the battery for more than 6,000 cycles to 80% of original capacity and gives a 5-year warranty. EcoFlow's 5 years requires app registration (3-year standard plus 2 years).
wins.who: BLUETTI (maker claim, also listed by APH Networks); EcoFlow store text

weak.claim: Heaviest of the 2 kWh group, so it carries less energy per pound. Arithmetic: 38.8 Wh/lb, against 51.7 (Jackery 2000 v2, 39.5 lb), 48.8 (Anker C2000 Gen 2, 42 lb) and 45.5 (DELTA 3 Max, 45 lb).
No expansion battery support. The Anker C2000 Gen 2 expands to 4 kWh and the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max Plus to 2–10 kWh.

Slower AC recharge than EcoFlow and Anker. CleanTechnica measured 0–100% in about 1 h 52 min, against BLUETTI's claim of 1.4 h. The Solar Lab measured 68 min on the DELTA 3 Max and about 88 min on the Anker C2000 Gen 2.

No surge rating is published; the 3,900 W figure is 'Power Lifting', for resistive loads only. Rival makers publish surge figures: DELTA 3 Max 4,800 W, Jackery 4,400 W, Anker 4,000 W. In testing, APH Networks saw the unit shut down with an error after about 5 s at 3,140 W (two hair dryers). CleanTechnica overloaded it at 3,300 W and it shut off and needed a reset.
Wall-to-outlet losses. StorageReview measured 1.91 kWh out and 2.44 kWh in to refill (arithmetic: about 78% round trip). The 1.91 kWh is about 92% of rated capacity, below APH's 97.8%.

Weak for RVs and vehicle charging. The Gadgeteer lists the missing 30 A RV plug as a con. Car-socket input is only 96 W at 12 V (arithmetic: about 21.6 h of driving to refill the rated capacity) unless you buy the Charger 1 bundle. The Gadgeteer also calls the 15 ms UPS switchover 'on the edge of being too long'; EcoFlow claims 10 ms.
weak.figure: No TT-30 outlet; 96 W car input; 15 ms UPS

weak.claim: Reviewer complaints and a caveat about the evidence. The Solar Lab lists BLUETTI's own panels as overpriced, a dated app, a dim screen in direct sun and no built-in light. It also says BLUETTI 'doesn't allow reviewers to criticize its products', so treat glowing BLUETTI reviews with care. CleanTechnica measured case temperatures of 110.8–116.2 °F under load.
weak.figure: Qualitative cons (The Solar Lab); 116.2 °F under load (CleanTechnica)

weak.claim: BLUETTI's own product page gives the capacity two ways: 2,080 Wh in the feature list and 2,073.6 Wh in the title. Use 2,073.6 Wh.

wins_for: Running a fridge, CPAP, router or reptile heat overnight with the inverter left on, where the 9.5 W idle draw (lowest of four units in The Solar Lab's tests) leaves the most energy for the load
Recharging mainly from solar: its 1,000 W input is the highest in the 2 kWh group at this price
Running several large appliances at once (2,600 W continuous) for about $900
Shoppers who want a 2 kWh station for the lowest price per watt-hour and won't need to add batteries later
not_for: Carrying it any distance (tent camping, tailgating, apartment stairs): at 53.4 lb it is the heaviest; the Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 (39.5 lb, $999) or the Anker C2000 Gen 2 (42 lb) are better
Home backup you plan to grow: it cannot take expansion batteries; the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max Plus ($1,149, 2–10 kWh) or the Anker C2000 Gen 2 (up to 4 kWh) are better
Fast refills from a generator or wall outlet between outages: the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max did 0–100% in 68 min (The Solar Lab), against about 1 h 52 min measured for the Elite (CleanTechnica)

Starting motors with a high surge (well pumps, some compressors): no surge rating is published and it shut down at 3,140 W (APH); choose a model whose maker publishes a surge figure, such as the DELTA 3 Max (4,800 W, maker claim)
Plugging straight into an RV's 30 A inlet: there is no TT-30 outlet (The Gadgeteer)
The cheapest 2 kWh at list price: the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max is $879, $20 less (though it idles at 27 W and takes only 500 W of solar)

rivals.where_it_beats_ours: $20 cheaper; 68 min 0–100% AC recharge (The Solar Lab); 45 lb; publishes a 4,800 W surge figure; 10 ms auto-switch (maker). Loses on idle draw (27 W), efficiency (79%) and solar input (500 W), and also cannot expand (The Solar Lab).

rivals.model: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max Plus (2,048 Wh, 3,000 W)
rivals.where_it_beats_ours: Expandable from 2 to 10 kWh; 3,000 W continuous / 6,000 W surge; 0–80% in 43 min on generator charging (maker claims). Costs $250 more.

rivals.price: $999 (compare-at $1,899), sold out, pre-order ships Nov 16, https://www.jackery.com/products/jackery-explorer-2000-v2-portable-power-station, read 2026-11-15
rivals.where_it_beats_ours: 39.5 lb against 53.4 lb; publishes a 4,400 W surge figure. Loses on idle draw (17 W), solar input (400 W), continuous output and price (The Solar Lab; maker).

rivals.model: Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 (2,048 Wh, 2,400 W)
rivals.price: $1,499.00 on https://www.anker.com/products/c2000-gen2, read 2026-11-15 (The Solar Lab reviewed it at $799; ankersolix.com rate-limited my check)
rivals.where_it_beats_ours: Expands to 4 kWh; 42 lb; about 88 min 0–100% (The Solar Lab); 4,000 W peak (maker). Loses on idle draw (~18 W), efficiency (~89%) and solar input (800 W).
Takes B300K/B500K expansion batteries (maker store). Not buyable today.
